title: Bootstrap SoringP1 Lean research foundation
body:
## Summary
- Establish pinned Lean 4.34 / Mathlib project, decision-tree formal model, and kernel-replay CI.
- Define the comparison-sorting number S(n) as the infimum of feasible worst-case decision-tree heights, with explicit outstanding existence/correspondence obligations.
- Specify unary and binary evaluation problems and threshold decision languages without incorrectly claiming that a numerical function belongs to NP.
- Record the partial-order minimax 2^{O(n²)} upper-bound sketch, its unary EXPTIME and binary 2-EXPTIME interpretations, and exploration-first research plan.

## Verification
The branch is ready for GitHub Actions CI; Lean could not be compiled in the current local environment. The Lean code intentionally contains no sorry/admit/axiom declarations.

## Research status
**Bootstrap only.** No P/NP membership, separation, or Lean-checked exponential runtime theorem is claimed.

## Note
The model currently specifies S via an infimum; a correctness/existence theorem and an executable evaluator remain explicit future milestones.

title: Add exact small-n minimax evaluator and regression tests
body: Adds a pure-Python reference implementation of the partial-order minimax recurrence, regression cases S(0..6)=0,0,1,3,5,7,10, and CI verification. This is deliberately **computational evidence**, not a Lean proof or complexity-class lower bound. Tested locally with n≤6. The Lean library and research roadmap remain unchanged except for a documented evaluator entry point.

title: Adopt exploration-first SoringP1 research workflow
body:
## Research direction

Make literature-led mathematical exploration the **operative default** for SoringP1 and its autonomous agents. Preserve the existing checked Lean foundation; stop automatically producing routine Lean milestones. Pursue structural minimax compression, certificate/hardness constraints, and combinatorial obstructions.

## Changes

- Update `AGENTS.md` to direct autonomous agents toward independent mathematics, literature audits, experiments, and falsification, not theorem counts.
- Replace the theorem-queue roadmap and formalization plan with explicit go/no-go criteria for further Lean.
- Add `docs/exploration-agenda.md`: audited sorting-number baseline, known strict inequality at n=12, sparsity of `SORT-BOUND-U`, and Mahaney's conditional barrier for ordinary many-one NP-hardness.
- Correct stale documentation about already proved small values, attainment, and the unfinished minimax height specification.
- Leave *all* Lean files, evaluator code, and CI unchanged.

## Verification

Documentation-only diff; GitHub Actions PR CI should still run `python -m unittest`, `lake build --wfail`, and `leanchecker`. Merge with **squash** to keep a signed GitHub-generated commit on `main`; the connector's working-branch commits are unsigned.

## Deployment scope

The repository is not a hosted application: merging to `main` publishes the research/agent instructions. Any Antonina board updates and Viche process refresh on `phoebe-dev` need to be carried out and verified separately; this PR does not claim those effects.

title: Bound exact sorting-number computation by deterministic budgeted DFS
body: Research-first upper bound: exact `CanSort(P,d)` uses OR over incomparable comparisons and AND over outcomes, depth d and O(n²) branching, yielding a uniform deterministic `2^{O(n (log n)^2)}`-time, polynomial-space algorithm for computing S(n) via binary search up to merge-sort bound. Sharper than memoized poset DP `2^{O(n²)}`. Distinguishes unary vs binary n, original result is paper deduction rather than Lean theorem and does not classify P/NP. Companion bounded pure Python DFS and CI tests (17/17 local tests passed). Peer-reviewed claims: only worst-case upper bounds, no asymptotic lower bound or per-instance speedup, binary 2^{2^{O(N)}} upper bound, no resource-heavy search, no claimed novelty. All commits signed on Phoebe; full CI and mathematical review required before merge.

title: Falsify poset-module reversal symmetry at n=7; retain restricted theorem
body: Research-first, Phoebe-only signed branch. Exhaustive n<=6 tests show module reversal seems value-invariant, but a reproducible n=7 isomorphism-quotient computation finds eight counterexamples, ruling out naive module/MDT state compression. Documents interval-module restricted invariance and experimental caveats; independent review requested especially for the interval-module proof (outside-outside incomparable moves must be addressed) and computational claims. No Lean or class-separation claim.

comments.body: **Mathematical review (2026-10-18):** Corrected/restricted optimal-merge formula matches Stockmeyer–Yao 1980, DOI 10.1137/0209006 (m≤n≤⌊3m/2⌋+1). The signed e2ed4a5 revision strengthens the lower bound to Σ_i ⌈log₂ e(P_i)⌉ + Σ_i δ_i for ordinal-sum factors. title: Analyze strategy-DAG certificates and relabelling quotients
body: Exploration-first research, all signed commits and local tests pass. Studies one-policy vs all-optimal strategy DAGs, verifies labelled-state injectivity for a reduced comparison tree, measures n<=6 state counts, and gives a polynomial-in-certificate-size verifier. Reviewed and corrected: multi-move DAG min/max semantics, explicit relabelling witnesses for quotient edges, verifier complexity and height check, no need for graph-isomorphism search when maps supplied, no finite-sample asymptotic assertions, no NP membership claim. Independently review mathematical details; CI required prior to merge.

comments.author: ottojung
comments.body: **Mathematical review (2026-10-18):** One reduced deterministic sorting policy cannot gain sharing by hash-consing identical labelled posets; relative to a fixed policy, different reachable nodes are distinct poset states. An S_n-quotient certificate can include explicit permutations as witnesses for each successor, so checking it does NOT require graph-isomorphism search; however its size is not known polynomial and this gives NO NP-membership result. The revised verifier includes both adversary outcomes, choice of move, terminal and height checks and conservative polynomial cost. Independent audit passed, with only editorial caveats; CI pending.

title: Benchmark sound polynomial-space pruning of exact budgeted DFS
body: Exploration-first, Phoebe-only signed research branch. Adds independent prototype and tests for capped DFS counting of linear extensions, Hanamura–Iwata seven-extension base, automorphism orbit pruning, and ordinal-sum allocation. Separates recursive call counts from actual runtime and retains polynomial space for capped enumeration; reference budgeted_dfs.py unchanged. Experimental n<=5 improvements only, no stronger worst-case asymptotic complexity claimed. Independently review capped-enumerator complexity and benchmarking methodology. CI required.

comments.author: ottojung
comments.body: **Mathematical review (2026-10-18):** Capped linear-extension enumeration is a sound information-bound prune using polynomial *space*; Hanamura–Iwata 2011 confirms e(P)≤7 implies a 3-comparison completion. The 349× figure refers to n=5 recursive-call reductions, not a uniform asymptotic speedup or constant running time. Optional automorphism-orbit mode materializes n! permutations and is explicitly NOT polynomial-space; signed correction 2dbecec records that. title: Clarify binary-input complexity bounds and certificate limits
body: Research-first Phoebe-dev signed branch (26afa0a, 66a6f21). Documents input-size normalization for S(n)<=k, existing deterministic 2-EXPTIME time and EXPSPACE space upper bounds under binary n, alternating-game argument, sparse/unary reduction caveats, explicit-tree certificate limitations. Review corrections avoid unsupported n² space lower-bound conjecture, distinguish *project-proved* EXPSPACE upper from a worldwide best-known claim, and explicitly prove binary-language density with trivial yes inputs. No new separation or EXPTIME membership is asserted. Mathematical peer review and GitHub CI required before merge.

comments.author: ottojung
comments.body: **Independent mathematical review (Phoebe, Antonina #301): YES, no blocking flaw.** Verified the binary-size/alternation translation, EXPSPACE upper, lack of EXPTIME proof, sparse-unary vs dense-binary distinction, and certificate caveats. Reviewer requested explicit handling of n=0, n=1, k=0 and preprocessing of trivial yes/no instances; these are corrected in signed commit `a0027d5`. Unsupported state-size-to-space-lower-bound conjecture was removed earlier. No P/NP hardness or complexity-class separation is claimed. Merge only after the updated head's CI succeeds.

title: Add certified constructive upper witnesses for poset sorting
body: Phoebe-only signed research branch 3f33a27, resumed after the free-model endpoint interrupted the original agent. Defines polynomial-numeric-time bound U_BIPI(P)=Σ_{k=1}^{n−1} min(m_k,ceil log₂(k+1)), with m_k the number of preceding keys incomparable to insertion key under a fixed linear extension. Proof: ordinary binary insertion into a dynamically sorted prefix skips comparisons already implied by the original poset; any insertion visits at most ceil log₂(k+1) distinct predecessors and pays for at most m_k. Combine with classical Ford–Johnson M(n) as U(P)=min(M(n),U_BIPI(P)); safe YES-prune if budget≥U(P). Includes explicit scripts, a regression correcting an earlier chain-order bug, and 13/13 passing local tests (14.7s). Empirical n≤5 validation, no improved uniform exact time bound or P/NP claim. Request independent mathematical review (especially BIPI proof and Ford–Johnson implementation) and green GitHub CI before merge.

comments.author: ottojung
comments.body: **Independent extended verification (Phoebe, current signed head 3f33a27):** In addition to the 13 passing committed tests, I enumerated **all 5,040 input permutations at n=7 and all 40,320 at n=8** for `fj_sort`; every output was correctly sorted, and maximum comparisons were exactly `M(7)=13`, `M(8)=16`. I also checked 65 deterministic random partial orders each at n=6 and n=7 using the separate BIPI simulator; in all 130, the policy sorted correctly and its observed worst-case cost did not exceed the proposed `U_BIPI(P)`. These bounded tests supplement, not replace, the paper proof of the general upper bound. Reviewer verdict and GitHub CI still apply before merge.

title: Prove one-ply adversarial information bound and infinite strict-witness family
body: Signed Phoebe-dev branch 38aea86 + 36f9f48, research-first. Proves L0(P)=ceil log2 e(P) <= L1(P)=1+min_pair max(L0(Pleft),L0(Pright)) <= F(P). Explicit smallest strict n=5 witness W=(26,0,10,0,8), e(W)=8,L0=3,L1=4,F=4, all first-pair splits 5/3 or 6/2. Extends to an infinite family W⊕C_t for all t>=0 via ordinal-sum additivity, unchanged extension counts and first-pair splits. Derives sound budget-d reject prune by capped linear-extension enumeration in O(2^d n²) time and polynomial space; carefully distinguishes that proposed prune from the included finite-experiment code (which uses exponential-space downset counting). Tests 9/9 pass in ~0.1s (all n<=4 plus witness and bounded n5 samples), no exhaustive expensive n5 F or complexity-class claim. Request independent mathematical/code review and green GitHub CI before merge.

title: Show asymmetric posets retain quadratically many comparison-pair orbits
body: Phoebe-only signed commit f1bf25d, exploration-first mathematical negative result. Construct height-two staircase posets P_m on n=2m keys with B_i<T_j iff j<=i. Every key is fixed by all automorphisms (distinct in/out degrees), but exactly 3*binom(m,2)=Theta(n²) pairs are incomparable and hence singleton candidate-comparison orbits; extend to odd sizes by appending a global maximum. Therefore **automorphism-orbit reduction alone cannot guarantee subquadratic pair branching for all poset states**. IMPORTANT: this is NOT an Ω(n²) time lower bound for deciding sorting numbers and does not rule out other structural/pruning algorithms or prove a class separation. Self-contained code and 6 bounded tests pass (n<=8 brute-force automorphism verification). Independent mathematical review and green GitHub CI required before merge.

title: Quantify exact winning-state advice tradeoffs in small sorting games
body: Signed Phoebe-only branch 8a0cca2, small n<=5 research prototype inspired by Stober–Weiß ALENEX2023 (arXiv:2206.05597). Enumerates *reachable* labelled poset states only (not arbitrary 2^(n!) permutation subsets), computes memoized exact F once to supply a partial confirmed-YES advice table, then measures un-memoized forward DFS with YES shortcut and crucial UNKNOWN != FALSE soundness. n5 partial budget B=5 yields 82,913 vs 107,659 forward nodes; B=6 yields 3 forward nodes but full precomputation is substantial and excludes construction cost from reported forward-node comparison. All five quick unit tests passed. **Epistemic warning:** This does NOT implement Stober–Weiß's actual predecessor-enumerating backward search, efficiency-threshold Lemma 4.2 completeness, or polynomial-space algorithm. It is a labelled precomputed-winner advice surrogate and a practical negative assessment, not a new speedup theorem or improved upper bound. Require independent math/code review and green CI before merge.

comments.author: ottojung
comments.body: Independent Phoebe peer audit (Antonina #301): substantive verdict YES, after addressing three review caveats. Signed correction e84dfb6 renames the toy `backward_table` as precomputed winning-state advice, states that all forward-node reduction ratios exclude precomputation, and accurately reproduces Stober–Weiß §4.2 Lemma 4.2: absence below the efficiency threshold implies NO only when a genuine partial-backward search satisfies its coverage hypotheses. Our toy implements neither predecessor enumeration nor that NO rule. All 5 targeted tests passed after amendment. Await updated-head GitHub CI before merge.

title: Prove compositional one-ply bounds and unbounded fixed-lookahead gap

comments.author: ottojung
comments.body: **Research-direction triage (founder-authorized, 2026-10-18):** Mathematical work remains valuable (factorwise one-ply lower bounds, the seven-key strict witness, and the unbounded gap family). But it does not currently imply a tighter uniform bound, a succinct certificate, or hardness for computing the special S(n). Under the founder's new complexity-first research policy, we are **archiving rather than integrating** this supporting result. The signed branch and all discussion remain available; this is not a rejection of the theorem. Reopen only if a concrete new bridge to the computational complexity of S(n) emerges.

title: Analyze adversarial lookahead hierarchy and first two-ply obstruction
body: Signed Phoebe research: formalize paper-level monotonicity, Lr<=L0+r, finite convergence to exact minimax; reproduce exhaustive n<=5 and offline n6 experiment, small n6 witness P=(0,0,0,1,3,27), e=30,L0=L1=5,L2=F=6, with fast CI tests. No hardness or complexity-class claim. Independent math and CI review before merge.

comments.author: ottojung
comments.body: **Major theorem correction, signed head `20151f2`.** Independent review originally accepted the paper's finite-convergence argument, but a further proof audit found two important errors: (1) bounding the number of distinct integer values does *not* bound the stabilization iteration by `max_P(F(P)-L0(P))`; the n=6 witness `(48,0,0,0,0,0)` already contradicts this intuition. (2) 'Whether L∞=F' is **not open**: in fact a strong universal theorem holds for all finite posets, `min(F(P),r+1) ≤ L_r(P) ≤ F(P)`. Proof by induction: base L0≥1 for nonterminal P; for each pair at least one child has F≥F(P)−1 by exact minimax, and the bound propagates. Hence `L_r(P)=F(P)` whenever `r≥F(P)−1`, and uniformly by `r≥S(n)−1`. The new paper proves this, corrects §4/6–8 and includes explicit regression refuting the old iteration bound. **12 targeted tests passed**, signed amended branch pushed. No P/NP/EXPTIME conclusion: high lookahead remains expensive. Please use *latest* CI on `20151f2` prior to merge.

comments.author: ottojung
comments.body: **Research-direction triage (founder-authorized, 2026-10-18):** The signed branch now contains the general finite convergence proof for lookahead and supporting n=6 witnesses. Its mathematical insight is preserved, but calculating further L_r values for arbitrary posets has no demonstrated asymptotic or classification consequence for S(n). We are **archiving this PR without merging** under the new exploration-first policy, not disputing the proof. Reopen if the hierarchy leads to a genuine new algorithmic bound or classification insight for the one-parameter S(n) problem.

title: Reduce exact sorting-number evaluation to O(n log² n) work space
body:
## Exceptional theoretical result about the special S(n)

The existing exact budgeted minimax DFS takes `2^{O(n log² n)}` time. Represent its state as a shared mutable comparison transcript and evaluate partial-order comparability by graph reachability on demand. A stack depth of `d ≤ O(n log n)` and O(log n) cursor/transcript data per level, plus one O(n log n) reachability workspace, give O((d+n)log(n+2)) bits per budgeted query and **O(n log²(n+2)) bits overall**. Previously the repository recorded `O(n³ log n)` from copying a full n×n relation per frame. This is a strictly improved uniform *space* bound, not an improvement in P/NP/PSPACE classifications or in the time exponent.

The same approach for an explicitly encoded, read-only **dense transitive-comparability matrix** of length N gives GEN-SORT in `DSPACE(O(√N log² N))` (encoding-sensitive, not a hardness statement).

## Review and validation

- Paper-level argument independently checked on Phoebe by a separate research agent, with explicit adversarial review of acyclicity, backtracking and input encodings.
- Independent scratch evaluator checked S(0..5) and 953 generalized-poset budget checks for n≤4 against a separate minimax oracle.
- Signed branch `cdc1bf8` corrects the first draft's actual implementation-level space defects (no O(n²) incomparable-pair list per recursion frame, no copied comparison transcript), corrects the d-small auxiliary-space accounting, and removes the generating-DAG versus transitive-matrix ambiguity.
- Nine targeted unit tests and git diff --check pass on Phoebe; pending full CI and additional final review before merge.

This is an asymptotic **space** refinement, not a P/NP classification, separation or claimed lower bound. References and code model in `docs/research-budgeted-dfs.md` and `scripts/transcript_dfs.py`.

title: Require 10+ parallel unary research agents; defer binary complexity
body:
Founder-directed, AssemblyP1-inspired research orchestration policy for SoringP1.

- Require **at least ten concurrently active, independent SoringP1 research agents**, all on `phoebe-dev`. Ten is a minimum, not a cap; replenish completed and failed investigations from a diversified research frontier.
- **Unary first, exclusively:** the active problem is `SORT-BOUND-U = {1^n#1^k : S(n)≤k}` and the unary function. Do **not** research the binary variant before the unary program is complete and the founder explicitly changes scope. Existing binary definitions and bounds remain as background only.
- Emphasize unary descriptive complexity: FO(LFP)/P, ESO/NP, FO(PFP)/PSPACE, and SO(LFP)/EXPTIME, with the distinction between generic capturing and a faithful explicit defining sentence.
- Explore the Ford–Johnson vs information lower bound gap to improve **threshold test cost**, alongside structural compression, certificates, reductions and source audits.
- Remove conflicting 'pause'/'do not saturate' instructions without creating quotas of Lean theorems or PRs. Align `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `docs/problem.md`, `docs/research-plan.md`, `docs/exploration-agenda.md`, and the new `docs/research-orchestration.md`.

Three signed commits, latest `0622741` verified on GitHub. No Lean code changed; the latest-head GitHub Actions run is being checked. Operationally, the Phoebe pool was redirected to unary-only and a separate orchestrator was started to replenish research agents.

title: Sharpen unary SORT-BOUND-U to 2^O(N log N) time and O(N log N) space
body:
**Uniform encoding-specific upper bound** for the *unary threshold decision* language. With `N=n+k+1` actual input symbols, read-only input and working bits, first accept when `k` exceeds a constructive sorting bound, else call budgeted transcript DFS at depth `d=k`. At most `n(n-1)` children per node, depth `k`, polynomial-cost node checks, and `(k+n)log(n+2)` working bits yield:

`SORT-BOUND-U ∈ DTIME(2^{O(N log N)}) ∩ DSPACE(O(N log N))`.

The existing bound for the **numeric unary function** `S_unary(1^n)` remains `2^{O(n log² n)}` time and `O(n log² n)` space because the algorithm invokes threshold tests at budgets `Θ(n log n)`. This is a derived sharpening of how to account for the threshold input length, not a new algorithm or a P/NP result.

Updates the derivation in `docs/research-budgeted-dfs.md`, plus accurate statements in `docs/problem.md` and `README.md`. Signed GPG commit `d85bd1f`; `git diff --check` passed. Please independently audit the input-length and polynomial per-node cost analysis before merging. Source model correspondence: `SoringP1/Minimax.lean`.

comments.author: ottojung
comments.body:
Independent Phoebe mathematical review of PR #29 — **APPROVE (mathematical bounds)**.

I independently rechecked the proof and a separate agent (510a18001228) audited the patch. The key points hold:
- Unary threshold input has length N=n+k+1. For k >= constructive U(n), return YES; otherwise run CanSort(∅,k), not a function-evaluation search at the worst-case budget.
- At most n(n−1) recursive calls per non-total node, depth at most k, with polynomial-time reachability/totality tests. Thus time 2^{O(k log(n+2))} poly(N) = 2^{O(N log N)}.
- A single transcript/DFS stack holds O((k+n)log(n+2)) bits; input is read-only. Thus workspace O(N log N).
- Base cases n=0,1 and the distinction from computing S_unary(1^n) were checked.
- GPG commit d85bd1f is verified; CI's reference-evaluator job passed, Lean build still pending at review time.

**Finite-model-theory terminology clarification:** VAR[3] is *not* the plain 3-variable FO fragment FO³. In Immerman's iterated-quantifier formalism, on ordered finite structures VAR[k+1]=DSPACE(N^k); thus VAR[3]=DSPACE(N²), and our upper bound does imply VAR[3]. See [Immerman's descriptive-complexity overview](https://people.cs.umass.edu/~immerman/descriptive_complexity.html). This does not imply VAR[2]=DSPACE(N).

**Verdict:** The deterministic time/space claims are sound. This is a sharper accounting of the existing evaluator for the unary threshold input, not P/NP membership or separation. Merge after the latest-head CI passes.

(Note: the independent agent's unauthenticated GitHub POST returned no comment ID and did *not* publish its claimed approval; this is the verified review record.)

title: Document Sergeev's sublinear sorting excess and entropy balance identity
body:
Core mathematical literature correction. Sergeev ECCC TR20-096 (2020), Theorem 3, proved `S(n)=log₂(n!)+O(n/(log n)^(1/5))`; our docs previously misleadingly said only linear gap and the excess asymptotics were open. His group-insertion sorting algorithm gives an asymptotic comparison-count upper bound, NOT a polynomial-time exact evaluator or directly evaluable finite constants. Add source and distinguish these questions.

Also record an elementary conditional-entropy balance identity for any correct sorting decision tree: `k−log₂(n!) = E[k−D]+Σ_v q_v(1−h₂(p_v))`. This gives a bound on the **expected** number of significantly biased comparisons under Sergeev's comparison bound, not any worst-case-path pruning or complexity separation.

Documentation-only signed commit `bcb69e8`; diff check clean. Request independent primary-source and mathematical review before merge. All work on Phoebe; active research remains unary-only and target five agents.

title: Prove a superlarge winning sorting frontier via independent chain comparisons
body:
**Updated, stronger paper-level theorem** (signed head `7efe8ca`, not yet independently approved or merged). The original two-edge binary-shift construction was unnecessarily elaborate. A simpler construction takes `s` disjoint already-sorted chains each of length `L`, established by `t₀=s(L−1)` adjacent-level comparisons. Each of the `M=(L−1)s(s−1)` other adjacent-level pairs is an **independent legal comparison**, giving `binom(M,m)` distinct labelled states at common depth `t=t₀+m`.

The `s` original chains remain sorted regardless of which extra edges were learned, and tournament merging needs at most `B=(s−1)+(sL−1)ceil(log₂s)` comparisons. Set `k=ceil(log₂((sL)!))` and choose `m=k−t₀−B`; then every constructed state is reachable and **winning** within `k−t=B`. Dividing by at most `(sL)!` labellings gives the non-isomorphic count.

**Exact new finite witness, with no floating-point arithmetic:** `s=16`, `L=14`, `n=224`, `k=1431`, `t₀=208`, `B=907`, `m=316`, `M=3120`, and `binom(3120,316)>2^39·224!`. Thus **more than `2^39` genuinely winning non-isomorphic states** at depth `524`. At `n=256`, `s=L=16`, the same count exceeds `2^148`. Asymptotically for `s=L=2^r`: count `2^((1/4−o(1))n(log₂n)²)`.

This excludes only algorithms that explicitly enumerate **every** reachable winning state modulo isomorphism; it does NOT prove a time lower bound for arbitrary unary S(n) algorithms, let alone class separation. Includes rigorous paper derivation, finite counts and adjacent-edge-independence tests (3/3 passing). Independent mathematician/agent peer review and latest-head CI required before merge; see Antonina #301.

Research agent `510a18001490` read the **current** PR #32 files (head `7efe8ca`), independently recomputed the full argument with arbitrary-precision integers, and performed exhaustive small-poset checks. I inspected its completed mathematical review and checked the proof separately.

- All `s(L−1)` initial chain edges are legal. All `M=(L−1)s(s−1)` other adjacent-level relations are independent: paths only increase the level, so a relation across one level cannot be transitively implied by another path. Exhaustive enumeration for rectangles `(s,L)=(3,3),(2,4),(4,2)` confirmed every subset gives a different poset.
- Each resulting state preserves the `s` known chains. Winner-tree merging proves `F(P_A)≤(s−1)+(n−1)ceil(log₂s)=B`. The reviewer also ran independent exact small-poset minimax checks.
- With `m=ceil(log₂(n!))−s(L−1)−B`, all `binom(M,m)` states lie at depth `t=k−B` and are genuinely winning within the residual budget. Quotienting by at most `n!` labellings is valid.
- Exact factorial/binomial arithmetic independently confirms **`binom(3120,316)>2^39·224!`** at `n=224`, and **`binom(3600,409)>2^148·256!`** at `n=256`.
- For `s=L=2^r`, `m=nr−O(n)` and `log₂(M/m)=r−O(log r)`, giving **`(1/4−o(1))n(log₂n)^2`** in the exponent.

**Scope audit:** This bounds the size of the full *winning state frontier*, not the running time or space of *all* algorithms deciding unary `SORT-BOUND-U`. The root may be losing, and selective symbolic search can escape enumeration.

**Verdict:** mathematically sound paper-level theorem. Not Lean-kernel-checked. Latest-head GitHub CI is a separate required gate; merge only on success.

title: Record unconditional EXPTIME sparsity barrier for unary sorting threshold
body:
Mature source-grounded complexity classification boundary, unary-only. Berman & Hartmanis, *On Isomorphisms and Density of NP and Other Complete Sets* (SIAM J. Comput. 6(2), 1977, DOI 10.1137/0206023) prove no polynomially sparse language is EXPTIME-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions. `SORT-BOUND-U` has at most `N` valid/accepted strings of each input length `N` (and at most `O(N²)` up to length `N`), and the existing exact DFS puts it in EXPTIME. Thus it is **unconditionally not EXPTIME-hard under polynomial-time many-one reductions**. This repairs an earlier research comment mistakenly saying 'at most one string per length'.

Carefully separates this unconditional EXPTIME non-hardness from conditional NP sparsity barriers (Mahaney), and from polynomial-time Turing reductions (not excluded). No P/NP membership or separation is claimed, and the result is marked literature + deduction rather than Lean-kernel-checked. Signed commit `f53b118` on Phoebe, `git diff --check` clean, all 8 targeted `test_hardness_boundaries.py` regressions passed. Request independent verification against the primary theorem and full CI before merging.

title: Correct unary hardness error; AC⁰ circuits and sharp one-comparison no-go
body:
**Research correctness correction (not a Lean milestone).** This PR updates only `docs/research-encoding-consequences.md`; no Lean source was added.

1. **Fix a false sparse NP-hardness example.** The old text treated φ↦1^{⟨φ⟩} as a polynomial-time many-one reduction from SAT. Under conventional binary Gödel coding its output is exponentially long. The unary-padded SAT example is actually in P by decoding an O(log N)-length formula and brute-forcing it in time polynomial in its unary input length N. Replaced with a concrete decidable tally language outside P, using polynomial-time-decodable repeated-machine diagonalization in (2^{O((log n)^2)}) time; it remains in P/1.

2. **Theorem 3.10: `SORT-BOUND-U∈nonuniform AC⁰`.** At any fixed length L, valid YES-instances `1^n#1^k` occupy an initial interval of delimiter positions because (n+S(n)) is strictly increasing. A depth-two DNF with O(L²) literals tests those positions. This does **not** give a uniform P or NP algorithm. As a restricted consequence, PARITY does not reduce to this unary threshold language by fixed-output-length nonuniform AC⁰ many-one reductions (Håstad's bound).

3. **Theorem 6.6: a tight *artificial* one-comparison-gap no-go function.** Let (I(n)=lceillog_2(n!)ceil). At the efficiently enumerable positions (t_m) where (I(n)-I(n-1)<lceillog_2 nceil), beyond index 8, encode the m-th bit of the tally diagonal H, setting (G(n)=I(n)+b_n) and (b_n=0) elsewhere. This (G) is computable, nondecreasing, obeys (I(n)le G(n)le I(n)+1), the insertion recurrence (G(n)le G(n-1)+lceillog_2 nceil), the standard merge recurrence (G(a+c)le G(a)+G(c)+(a+c-1)), and the same nonuniform depth-two AC⁰ property. Yet its **unary threshold is outside uniform P**: (1^{t_m}#1^{I(t_m)}) queries the m-th bit of H and has length polynomial in m. All-n proofs are included; the stronger merge-inequality constant is verified by Pascal's identity and the binomial row 9 bound.

**Critical limitation:** (G
e S) and none of this proves a complexity lower bound for actual optimal sorting. Instead it disproves proposed arguments that extrapolate uniform P from only numerical accuracy, monotonicity, insertion/merging upper recurrences, or nonuniform circuits. Real research priority is all-n structure of *optimal sorting strategies*; see issues #47 (complete checkable framed policies) and #48 (forcing root adversaries). No further routine Lean formalization should follow from this note.

Reviewer asks: carefully verify the diagonal enumeration, positive density and polynomial invertibility of permitted insertion slots, and the rounding in the merge inequality. Primary background: Mahaney, *JCSS* 1982; Håstad, STOC 1986.

title: Keep Lean verification for theorem changes; skip it for research-note-only PRs
body:
The SoringP1 research program intentionally forbids low-ROI Lean formalization, yet `.github/workflows/ci.yml` currently installs Lean/Mathlib and replays the entire kernel for **every docs-only research note**. PR #44 has already triggered several redundant 90-minute-capable Lean runs despite changing no Lean source.

This workflow-only change introduces a conservative **theorem-affecting-path gate** in the existing `lean` job, while keeping the lightweight Python `reference-evaluator` job unconditional:

- Run Lean whenever `SoringP1/`, `SoringP1.lean`, `lakefile.lean`, `lakefile.toml`, `lake-manifest.json`, `lean-toolchain`, or this workflow changes.
- Always run Lean on `workflow_dispatch`.
- For PRs compare against the actual base SHA; for pushes compare against the previous commit SHA, fetching the base at shallow depth. Missing/invalid/unfetchable SHA or failed diff **defaults to full Lean verification**, never silently skips it.
- Only for changes strictly outside Lean-relevant paths, complete the existing job successfully without installing Lean or downloading Mathlib; Python evaluator still runs in its normal job.
- On this workflow-changing PR itself, full Lean build *must* execute, validating that the guard cannot disable verification of its own implementation.

No Lean proofs are added, changed, or weakened. This is a targeted efficiency fix, not suppression of required kernel checking for actual Lean changes. Review the path regular expression and the PR merge-commit vs push-base selection carefully.

title: Add independent framed-DAG certificate checker (no Lean formalization)
body:
## Purpose
Concrete polynomial-time verifier for the **forgetful, permutation-framed comparison strategy DAG** from issue #47. A rigorous witness format is a prerequisite to asking whether optimal antichain-root policies admit polynomial certificates; this PR does **not** claim NP membership or optimal-policy completeness.

## Contents
- `scripts/check_framed_strategy.py`: topologically ordered DAG with two comparison outcomes and explicit slot permutations on both edges. Propagates the *intersection* of guaranteed relations over all incoming histories, using transitive closure after queries. Checks terminal states are total and longest reachable path is within the comparison budget.
- `triangular_bubble_certificate(n)`: all-n polynomial-size example with `n(n-1)/2` compare-exchange nodes; both branches share the next node via optional slot swaps.
- `tests/test_framed_strategy.py`: cases `n=0..12`, plus negative tests for wrong permutation, missing comparison work, budget violation, cyclic edges and malformed frames.

## Validation and scope
An equivalent checker was executed locally: all tests passed and bubble example for n=16 accepted with 120 comparisons, 121 nodes. See all-n paper proof in issue #47. Python reference tests will run in CI; no Lean source changed. Checker time is polynomial in explicit DAG size and **n**, appropriate for the *unary* `SORT-BOUND-U` target. As in issue #47, the open research problem is polynomial-size **completeness at exactly S(n)**, not soundness or ordinary upper-bound compression.

Closes no research issue; related to #47.

title: Consolidate research policy docs; stop the pool keeper from inventing filler work

The pool keeper enforced the floor by telling agents with exhausted packets to invent a new question, which is the filler pressure the docs warn against. Several docs were also stale.
